name: Ananya Sharma
text: This is a much-needed step towards protecting citizen data. Glad to see the government taking initiative on privacy.

name: Rohan Mehta
text: The consent framework is finally clear and transparent. Very supportive of this policy.

name: Priya Nair
text: As a startup founder, the compliance cost for a small company like ours is far too high. This will hurt innovation.

name: Arjun Reddy
text: Data localization requirements are excessive and will burden Indian companies competing globally.

name: Sneha Patil
text: Good move overall, but the grievance redressal timeline of 90 days is too long.

name: Vikram Singh
text: The exemption for research purposes is a welcome and progressive addition.

name: Meera Iyer
text: Concerned about how children's data will actually be protected in practice. The clause is too vague.

name: Karan Malhotra
text: This policy is confusing and poorly drafted. Needs a complete rewrite.

name: Divya Rao
text: Appreciate the effort but the penalty structure feels unfair to smaller enterprises.

name: Aditya Verma
text: Cross-border data transfer rules seem balanced and reasonable to me.

name: Neha Kulkarni
text: Finally some clarity on data governance. This is a positive step for the digital economy.

name: Suresh Pillai
text: The compliance burden on MSMEs has not been thought through at all. Disappointed.

name: Kavya Reddy
text: Transparency requirements are commendable and long overdue.

name: Ramesh Gupta
text: Why is there no mention of health data protection specifically? A major gap.

name: Ishita Sen
text: Supportive of the policy but implementation timeline of six months is unrealistic.

name: Manoj Kumar
text: This will help build public trust in how our data is used. Welcome move.

name: Pooja Joshi
text: The penalty amounts are excessive and could bankrupt small businesses.

name: Abhishek Das
text: Good policy in spirit, but the enforcement mechanism is weak.

name: Lakshmi Naidu
text: As a farmer, I don't see how this protects agricultural data collected by private apps. Needs more detail.

name: Rahul Bansal
text: The draft is a step in the right direction for citizen rights.

name: Anjali Deshmukh
text: Unclear how the grievance redressal officer will be appointed. Needs more transparency.

name: Sanjay Chauhan
text: This is exactly the kind of progressive data protection law we needed.

name: Tanvi Shah
text: Startups will struggle to comply with these localization requirements. Bad for the industry.

name: Nikhil Bose
text: Simple, clear and fair. A well-balanced policy overall.

name: Ritu Chandra
text: The consent mechanism is complicated for a layperson to understand.

name: Amitabh Tiwari
text: Great to see provisions for data portability included.

name: Swati Menon
text: Very concerned about surveillance implications hidden within this policy.

name: Deepak Yadav
text: Nice policy.

name: Shreya Kapoor
text: Good policy.

name: Harish Chandran
text: This clause on data localization is harmful to cloud businesses operating in India.

name: Nisha Agarwal
text: The research exemption clause could be misused by large corporations. Needs safeguards.

name: Farhan Ansari
text: Appreciate the public consultation process itself, it feels genuinely participatory.

name: Bhavna Trivedi
text: The draft lacks clarity on how penalties will be calculated for repeat violations.

name: Gaurav Saxena
text: A strong, welcome policy that puts citizens first.

name: Rekha Pandey
text: Compliance timelines are too tight for smaller companies to adapt.

name: Vivek Nambiar
text: Overall a fair and balanced approach to data governance.

name: Anita Hegde
text: The policy fails to address data collected through government welfare schemes.

name: Rajesh Thakur
text: This is a helpful and much-needed regulatory framework.
